title: Cracked doll shoulder holds its arm again — mesh and epoxy
description: This vintage baby doll's shoulder had cracked through at the arm socket. Fibreglass mesh and epoxy now reinforce the socket from inside, black-tinted epoxy fills the split, and the arm is back in place with a careful paint touch-up.
itemDetails: A vintage jointed baby doll with a glossy black moulded body and head. The hair is sculpted into the head in deep combed waves. It has bright yellow-green eyes, painted yellow brows, red painted lips, and gold-tone hoop earrings through the moulded ears. The arms are separate pieces with rounded shoulder ends that sit in sockets in the torso. It wears red fabric pants with white lace trim. No maker's mark is visible in the repair footage, so the manufacturer and date are not confirmed. Dolls of this style are often marked on the back of the neck or the body.
repairDetails:
The doll's shoulder had cracked at the arm socket. The split ran from the socket opening up toward the neck, leaving the joint too weak to hold the arm.

With the arm removed, a piece of fibreglass mesh is cut to size and worked through the socket opening. Clear two-part epoxy goes on with a toothpick, bonding the mesh across the inside of the crack as a hidden support.

A second batch of epoxy is tinted black and pressed into the split from the outside. Once it has cured, a flat file levels the repair and cleans up the rim of the socket so the arm can seat again.

The arm is pressed back into the shoulder. A fine brush then blends black paint over the repaired area to bring it closer to the doll's original finish.
